articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Mossdeep’s perfect season resumes against the team that came within three
articles.dek: Dewford returns with four straight wins, a healthy core and a 24–21 memory. The Eclipse begin the postseason with a much larger season-long case.

body.text: Dewford does not have to invent a reason to believe it can stay close to Mossdeep. The Breakers lost their Week 4 meeting 24–21, one of the few afternoons on which the Eclipse’s eventual perfect regular season looked seriously contested. Now they meet again, in Mossdeep, with a conference-final place available. The old score gives Dewford a starting point. The intervening season explains why the assignment remains so large.

Mossdeep finished 17–0, scoring 724 points and allowing 130. Dewford finished 11–6, then won 20–9 at Eterna in the wild-card round. The Breakers have won four straight, including a 35–29 finale victory at Rustboro. They have recently won with different kinds of production: a high-scoring road finish with a major return contribution, then a playoff game built around two short rushing touchdowns and a defense that never allowed the opponent into the end zone.

Michael Dorrill’s team has been waiting through the bye after a deliberate late-season rest policy. The coach confirmed that he was reducing starter injury exposure and giving younger players experience. That context belongs beside the Eclipse’s 22–3 win over Sootopolis and 27–0 shutout at Lavaridge. Those games cannot simply be treated as full-strength offensive auditions, and the divisional lineup should be confirmed from the actual selections rather than presumed from the finale.
The first meeting provides history, not a script

body.speaker: Michael Dorrill
body.text: We rested players because we wanted them ready for this work. That does not buy anybody an excuse for a missed assignment. Dewford already showed us it can stay in a game with us. We need to execute the next play correctly, then do it again.

The 24–21 result matters because it is an actual competitive meeting between these clubs. It does not tell us which later roster choices will be made or how the same players will perform after further development. Dewford’s useful lesson is that Mossdeep has already had to finish a close game against this opponent. Mossdeep’s useful lesson is equally concrete: the Breakers can create enough offense and field position to punish a careless afternoon.

The Eclipse’s season after that meeting provides a substantial counterweight. They beat Saffron 20–17, Rustboro 35–7, Petalburg 55–0 and Sunyshore 27–3. Their regular-season scoring margin reached plus-594. Those results establish a much broader performance record than the single close game in Dewford. The favorite’s case is built from repeated scoring and prevention, with the Week 4 score identifying a matchup worth taking seriously inside that record.

For Dorrill, the practical task is to restore the intended playoff roles without allowing the rest period to become an excuse for imprecision. His established standard leaves little room to celebrate ordinary competence as a special postseason achievement. The Eclipse earned home field so they could use it; their first elimination game still begins 0–0. A missed assignment will carry the same consequence whether it follows seventeen wins or a losing season.
Dewford must avoid a passing chase

Frosmoth completed eleven of sixteen passes for 105 yards against Eterna, with one interception and no touchdown passes. That was enough because Watchog scored twice on the ground and the defense held the Thorns to three field goals. A similar passing total could become much harder to live with if Mossdeep reaches twenty-one points early. Dewford needs its first several possessions to create useful field position and manageable downs, even when they do not immediately score.

Excadrill carried sixteen times for sixty-four yards in the wild-card win. Watchog added twenty-seven yards on seven carries, including the two five-yard touchdowns. Meowscarada contributed twenty-one yards on two rushes. Those roles gave the Breakers several ways to gain short and intermediate distances. Their challenge is to preserve that usefulness against a defense that allowed only 130 regular-season points, rather than asking Frosmoth to recover repeated long-yardage situations.

The quarterback’s regular season included 2,459 passing yards, twenty-six touchdowns and twelve interceptions. That line supports a credible passing contribution, but it also explains why possession security belongs near the top of Brawly’s preparation. An early interception at Eterna did not become an opposing touchdown. Mossdeep’s offensive production makes the same mistake potentially more expensive. Dewford cannot assume that another defensive rescue will keep the score unchanged.

Meowscarada’s return threat also deserves specific attention. The Breakers’ finale included a ninety-nine-yard kickoff-return touchdown against Rustboro. Mossdeep must prepare for field-position damage even on possessions where its defense has not yet taken the field. That is a checkable special-teams concern, not a forecast that the returner will repeat the play. Dewford’s strongest upset route includes making the Eclipse defend shorter fields than their season averages would ordinarily suggest.
Mossdeep has several established touchdown sources

Dram Marino finished the regular season with 4,341 passing yards, fifty-six touchdown passes and four interceptions. Accel BeckhmJr caught thirty-two touchdowns while gaining 1,953 receiving yards. Ninjaskamara rushed for 1,138 yards and twenty touchdowns. Gronkaludon contributed 830 receiving yards and nine scores, while Ninjulio Jones added 770 and seven. The volume is spread across enough roles to make a single-defender solution implausible.

Those are completed regular-season totals, separate from the postseason box scores. They also describe what the principal scorers have already done, rather than announcing the exact divisional depth chart. If the Eclipse return their main passing and rushing contributors to their expected work, Dewford has to defend several kinds of scoring pressure simultaneously. The Breakers cannot spend the entire game preventing one long reception while conceding every short rushing opportunity.

The Eterna result offers Dewford a useful defensive model at the level of outcomes: limit touchdowns, force difficult third downs and finish the late takeaway. The Breakers held the Thorns to one conversion in eight third-down attempts and intercepted Slowking with 2:20 left. Reproducing those outcomes against Marino is a much harder assignment. His four regular-season interceptions came alongside fifty-six touchdown passes, leaving opponents very little evidence of routine giveaways to rely on.

For Mossdeep, the offensive key is to turn its stronger production into actual touchdown possessions before the game becomes a return-and-field-goal contest. The 24–21 first meeting gives the home team no reason to be casual about missed opportunities. Dewford has just demonstrated that it can win a road elimination game with 225 total yards. The Eclipse should make the Breakers exceed that offensive demand rather than voluntarily leaving them a low target.
Availability and the final possession

Poury Holt remains listed with five weeks of recovery. His absence is confirmed; a specific replacement workload should come from the chosen lineup. Shawn Mareman’s earlier minor entry has cleared, and Richard Furman’s healthy designation does not by itself establish activation from injured reserve. Readers should distinguish a player being free of a recovery counter from a confirmed roster move or starting assignment.

Dewford has no positive-week injury among its current players in this export. Dusclops has a new minor entry with zero weeks remaining. That is a comparatively favorable report for a road team preparing to face a deeper scoring offense. It allows the Breakers to build around their available contributors without an additional confirmed absence from the wild-card game. It does not guarantee that every player will take the same role or workload again.

The winner will face either Sunyshore or Petalburg for the Hoenn–Sinnoh championship. Mossdeep would host that game as the top seed. Dewford, the fifth seed, would travel to either surviving division winner. Those paths explain the stakes without turning the divisional game into a preliminary formality. Both teams must earn the next fixture before its location matters.

My forecast is Mossdeep 35, Dewford 17. I expect the Breakers to create some offense through rushing and field position, with the earlier close meeting keeping the favorite attentive. The Eclipse’s passing efficiency and multiple established touchdown sources give them the stronger route to sustained scoring. Dewford’s upset requires the game to remain manageable long enough for its late-possession strengths to matter; Mossdeep’s task is to make that window smaller from the opening quarter.

articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Blackthorn returns to Mt. Silver with a passing game the Reds have already met
articles.dek: The Dragons won 30–22 here in Week 12. Hatterene’s five-touchdown opener raises the stakes for an injured top seed coming off its bye.

body.text: Blackthorn’s trip to Mt. Silver is a return visit to a place where the Dragons have already won. Their 30–22 victory in Week 12 gives this divisional game a specific history, and their 38–10 wild-card win at Cinnabar gives it immediate force. Hatterene arrives after five touchdown passes. The Reds arrive rested, at home and still dealing with several injuries that the bye did not fully resolve.

Mt. Silver earned the conference’s top seed with a 14–3 regular season, 481 points scored and 206 allowed. Blackthorn finished 12–5, scoring 385 and allowing 348. Those full-season records favor the Reds. The current matchup is less comfortable for them: Tic Thorpe still has two weeks reported, Josh Alakazam three, Tony Gyarzalez four, and Vibrava four. The top seed has a substantial season behind it and a narrower available group in front of it.

Garshawn Lynch is central to the home team’s answer. He led the league with 1,200 regular-season rushing yards, scored eleven rushing touchdowns and added four receiving scores. Blackthorn’s quarterback just won through repeated completions to several receivers. Mt. Silver’s clearest route is to sustain its own possessions, finish them and keep Hatterene from receiving a succession of extra opportunities against a defense forced back onto the field.
Hatterene has answered one difficult ending

body.speaker: Connor McLarren
body.text: Blackthorn has already won a game here, so I doubt they need help finding the entrance. We have earned the chance to give them a different afternoon. Garshawn has been giving people something to tackle all season. We will need the passing game to do its share, too, because Hatterene is unlikely to spend the day admiring our regular-season record.

The Dragons lost the Johto East finale 21–20 at Lavender on a last-second field goal. That defeat cost them the division and sent them to Cinnabar. They then entered halftime of the wild-card game tied 10–10 before scoring twenty-eight unanswered points. The response matters because it was observed: an early interception and a tied road game did not stop Hatterene from producing four second-half touchdown passes.

He completed twenty-eight of thirty-seven attempts for 367 yards. Grovyle caught all nine targets for 135 yards, Hawlucha caught three touchdowns and Simeon Ice caught two. The Dragons gained only ten rushing yards, with three closing kneels included in the total. Their win was carried by the passing game, supported by a defense that repeatedly stopped Cinnabar on third down and sacked Gholdengo four times.

That performance gives Mt. Silver several receiving problems to solve. Concentrating exclusively on the touchdown scorers would overlook Grovyle’s nine completions. Concentrating exclusively on yardage would overlook Hawlucha and Simeon Ice finishing drives. The Reds need to defend the full passing sequence: the early completion that creates a manageable down, the conversion that keeps a possession alive and the final throw near the end zone.

Hatterene’s regular-season totals reinforce the threat: 4,532 passing yards, thirty-eight touchdowns and eight interceptions. The wild-card line was an exceptional afternoon within an already substantial passing season. It should not be treated as a guaranteed repeat, especially against a stronger season-long defense. It does establish that Blackthorn can enter this rematch with a current offensive identity more specific than merely being a dangerous lower seed.
The Reds have a rushing answer and a quarterback question

Lynch’s production is the first reason to resist making the Dragons an automatic road choice. A runner who gained 1,200 yards can give the available quarterback shorter downs and can make Blackthorn defend stretches of offense rather than spend the afternoon preparing its next passing series. The Reds also beat Saffron 36–33 in Week 15. Their season includes a win over a contender capable of scoring at a much faster pace than Cinnabar managed in the wild-card round.

The recent results also include a 38–24 loss at Cinnabar and a 21–13 finale defeat against Cianwood. Those games should be read with the available personnel in mind, but the injury context does not erase the points conceded or the offensive limitations. Mt. Silver has to produce a working divisional plan from the players actually available. Its top seed does not restore an injured passer or a missing receiving target.

Crem Ftzpatrik completed the regular season with 1,004 passing yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. Tic Thorpe’s earlier work produced 1,560 yards, seventeen touchdowns and two interceptions, while Josh Alakazam and Jacoby Brizzet also contributed at quarterback. Those totals show a season divided among several passers. The preview should not quietly combine them into the performance of one healthy incumbent.

Tony Gyarzalez’s continuing absence removes a receiver who gained 948 yards and scored seven touchdowns during the regular season. Gregar Jenings produced 795 yards and six scores, Scep Smith Jr. added 633 and five, and Plusico Buress had 572 and four. There are remaining targets with recorded production. The question is whether the available quarterback and protection can connect with them often enough to keep pace with Hatterene.
A bye changes recovery, not every designation

Ninji Asomugha’s counter has reached zero after previously showing one week. That is a meaningful availability change, although it does not establish a particular starting assignment. Other absences remain positive: Ariados is listed for nine weeks and Medicham for three, alongside the quarterback, tight-end and backfield injuries. The Reds received a week without a game; they did not receive a fully cleared injury list.

Blackthorn’s Sawsbuck remains listed for three weeks. Exploud’s counter has reached zero after showing one. The returning designation could expand available options, but readers should wait for an actual role before assigning him a projected workload. The Dragons’ wild-card receiving distribution already gives us a confirmed account of how they functioned without assuming that every newly cleared player immediately resumed an old job.

This is why I prefer to frame the game around demands rather than a guessed formation. Blackthorn needs efficient passing and enough protection for Hatterene to use several receivers. Mt. Silver needs productive Lynch possessions and a passing contribution that does not give those possessions back through mistakes. Neither statement requires access to a private playbook, and both can be checked against the recorded game afterward.
The previous meeting makes the upset credible

The Week 12 result was Blackthorn 30, Mt. Silver 22 at the same home venue. It is evidence that the Dragons have already won this matchup on the road. It is not evidence that every matchup detail remains unchanged. Injuries, development and available roles have moved since then, and the divisional pressure changes the consequence of the result even when the field is familiar.

Mt. Silver’s strongest response would be to make the game feel different through its own offensive consistency. Lynch can reduce the frequency of long-yardage passing situations, while the remaining receivers can punish a defense that becomes too focused on the run. A home lead would allow the Reds to use that balance. An early two-score deficit would increase the burden on a quarterback group already missing important contributors.

Blackthorn’s defense has a recent success to carry forward: Cinnabar converted only two of eleven third downs and never scored after halftime. Vigoroth’s three sacks included a fourth-and-one stop that helped accelerate the third-quarter separation. The Reds will present a different rushing challenge from the Blaze, so those outcomes cannot simply be transferred. They do identify the kind of possession-ending plays that would make Hatterene’s task easier.

My forecast is Blackthorn 30, Mt. Silver 27. The Reds’ home field, rushing production and full-season defense keep this close. The Dragons have the clearer current passing performance and a prior win in the same matchup, while Mt. Silver’s continuing quarterback and tight-end absences make a late passing exchange harder. The winner reaches the Kanto–Johto championship game against Saffron or Lavender; Blackthorn would travel again, while a Mt. Silver win would preserve home field.
